[LLM] Node.js descendant queries AWS IMDS (169.254.169.254) or ECS task metadata (169.254.170.2) Actions on Objectives High
Hunts for the stage-2 Bun-compiled credential harvester querying the EC2 IMDSv2 endpoint or the ECS task metadata endpoint from a Node.js/npm/bun process context. This is the article's central credential-access TTP and is anomalous on developer workstations (where IMDS shouldn't resolve at all). Rationale: Combines the article's stage-2 behaviour (IMDS + ECS metadata queries) with the article-specific filenames (opensearch_init.js / ai_init.js / payload.bin) and Node/Bun runtime context. Detection is highest fidelity on developer workstations where 169.254.169.254 has no legitimate purpose.
ATT&CKT1552.005 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let TargetIPs = dynamic(["169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in (TargetIPs)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe","node","npm","bun")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","bun.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("opensearch_init.js","ai_init.js","payload.bin","preinstall.js","setup.mjs")
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, DeviceType, OSPlatform, IsInternetFacing) by DeviceId
  ) on DeviceId
| where OSPlatform !contains "Linux" or IsInternetFacing == false
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
let TargetIPs = dynamic(["169.254.169.254", "169.254.170.2"]);
let NetEvents = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (TargetIPs)
    | project NetTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, Url;
let NodeProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe","node","npm","bun")
         or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("opensearch_init.js","ai_init.js","payload.bin","preinstall.js","setup.mjs")
    | project ProcTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetUsername;
NetEvents
| join kind=inner NodeProcs on DvcHostname
| where NetTime between (ProcTime .. ProcTime + 10m)
| project NetTime, ProcTime, DvcHostname, TargetUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url
| order by NetTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 (@DestinationIp:169.254.169.254 OR @DestinationIp:169.254.170.2) (@Image:(*\node.exe OR *\Node.exe OR *\NODE.EXE OR *\npm.exe OR *\NPM.EXE OR *\bun.exe OR *\Bun.exe OR *\BUN.EXE) OR @CommandLine:(*opensearch_init.js* OR *ai_init.js* OR *payload.bin* OR *preinstall.js* OR *setup.mjs*))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.169.254" OR RemoteAddressIP4="169.254.170.2")
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/\\(node|npm|npx|bun)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/(opensearch_init\.js|ai_init\.js|payload\.bin|preinstall\.js|setup\.mjs)/i)}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], key=[aid, TargetProcessId])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())

[LLM] vpmdhaj campaign stager / payload artifact written under node_modules Installation High
Hunts for the article's specific stager and payload filenames (preinstall.js, setup.mjs, opensearch_init.js, ai_init.js, payload.bin, payload.gz) appearing under a node_modules path or matching the published SHA-256 hashes. Catches both the install-time drop and any artifact re-introduced later. Rationale: Combines the three article-published SHA-256 hashes with the article-specific filenames (opensearch_init.js, ai_init.js, payload.bin, payload.gz, preinstall.js, setup.mjs) constrained to node_modules paths. The filename+path combo catches re-bundles where hashes might change; the hash list catches direct copies.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let BadHashes = dynamic(["638788AFC4F1B5860A328312CAF5895ABD5F5632D28A4F2A85B09076E270D15D","77D92EFE7AF3547F71FD41D4A884872D66B1BE9499EAA637E91EAC866911694D","BFA149694EC6411C23936311A999163ADE54D6F38E2F4B0E3CFB8CB67BD7CFAA"]);
let BadNames = dynamic(["opensearch_init.js","ai_init.js","payload.bin","payload.gz","preinstall.js","setup.mjs"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where SHA256 in (BadHashes)
     or (FileName in~ (BadNames) and FolderPath has "node_modules")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
let BadHashes = dynamic(["638788AFC4F1B5860A328312CAF5895ABD5F5632D28A4F2A85B09076E270D15D","77D92EFE7AF3547F71FD41D4A884872D66B1BE9499EAA637E91EAC866911694D","BFA149694EC6411C23936311A999163ADE54D6F38E2F4B0E3CFB8CB67BD7CFAA"]);
let BadNames = dynamic(["opensearch_init.js","ai_init.js","payload.bin","payload.gz","preinstall.js","setup.mjs"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileSHA256 in (BadHashes)
     or (TargetFileName in~ (BadNames) and TargetFilePath has "node_modules")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] npm install lifecycle hook spawning detached Bun / Node child (vpmdhaj _DAEMONIZED marker) Installation Medium
Hunts for an npm install lifecycle hook spawning a detached Node.js or Bun child process that executes one of the campaign's stage-2 scripts. The article describes Gen-2 silently downloading the legitimate Bun runtime and running a pre-bundled script — this UC catches that parent-child shape. Rationale: Targets the article's distinctive process tree: npm/node parent → node/bun child running one of the six named stager filenames or carrying the _DAEMONIZED=1 marker. Constraining to node_modules path strips out unrelated legitimate Node tooling.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js","npm install","npm i ")
| where FileName has_any ("node.exe","bun.exe")
     or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("opensearch_init.js","ai_init.js","payload.bin","preinstall.js","setup.mjs","_DAEMONIZED")
     or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)bun\s+(run\s+)?\.\\?node_modules\\"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "node_modules" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules" or ProcessCommandLine has "node_modules"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe","bun.exe")
     or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm-cli.js","npm install","npm i ")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","bun.exe")
     or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("opensearch_init.js","ai_init.js","payload.bin","preinstall.js","setup.mjs","_DAEMONIZED")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "node_modules" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "node_modules"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: vpmdhaj npm Install Lifecycle Hook Spawns Bun/Node Stager
id: 7d2c9b4e-1a8f-4e2d-9c63-3b5e7a1f0d03
status: experimental
description: Detects npm/node parent processes spawning a Bun or Node child running one of the vpmdhaj campaign stage-2 scripts (opensearch_init.js, ai_init.js, payload.bin, preinstall.js, setup.mjs) or carrying the _DAEMONIZED marker.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/typosquatted-npm-packages-steal-cloud-and-ci-cd-secrets/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:

      - '\node.exe'

      - 'payload.bin'
      - 'preinstall.js'
      - 'setup.mjs'
      - '_DAEMONIZED'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_payload
level: high

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or SHA1 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa") or MD5 in~ ("638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["638788afc4f1b5860a328312caf5895abd5f5632d28a4f2a85b09076e270d15d", "77d92efe7af3547f71fd41d4a884872d66b1be9499eaa637e91eac866911694d", "bfa149694ec6411c23936311a999163ade54d6f38e2f4b0e3cfb8cb67bd7cfaa"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

New ChatGPT Vulnerability Lets Attackers Turn Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads

Cyber Security News
2026-05-29 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A browser-based prompt injection technique that transforms any web page into a phishing delivery surface by exploiting ChatGPT&#8217;s page summarization feature, rendering attacker-controlled links, fake security alerts, and QR codes directly inside the trusted ChatGPT interface. Researchers at Permiso have disclosed the attack dubbed ChatGPhish, which builds on the same trust-transfer logic previously demonstrated against [&#8230;] The post New ChatGPT Vulnerability Lets Attackers Turn Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ChatGPhish UI-redress click — browser navigation to rare external domain seconds after chatgpt.com summarize render · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — New ChatGPT Vulnerability Lets Attackers Turn Web Pages Into Phishing Payloads
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ChatGPhish passive tracking beacon — browser fetch to URL shortener immediately after chatgpt.com summarize session · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] ChatGPhish passive tracking beacon — browser fetch to URL shortener immediately after chatgpt.com summarize session Command & Control Low
Hunts for a user's browser making an outbound request to a URL-shortener domain (shorturl.at and peers) within minutes of fetching chatgpt.com from the same process. Targets the ChatGPhish 'passive tracking beacon' primitive where attacker-injected Markdown images embedded in a summarized page are auto-rendered by ChatGPT and leak the victim's IP/User-Agent/Referer/timing to attacker infra via a shortened URL hop. Rationale: Anchored on the two domains the article actually names — chatgpt.com (the trusted surface) and shorturl.at (the article-cited shortener used to embed Markdown image beacons). The temporal join (5-minute window from chatgpt.com fetch to shortener fetch by the SAME browser process) is what makes this article-specific rather than a generic 'browser to shortener' hunt. Corroborated against The Register's coverage which independently confirmed Permiso researcher Andi Ahmeti's QR-code / spoofed-alert / passive-beacon primitives. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/05/29/chatgpt-prompt-injection-turns-web-pages-into-phishing-lures/5248137 • https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102 T1659
Data sourcesWeb.Web

ChatGPTTime + 5m) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Browser=InitiatingProcessFileName, ShortenerUrl=RemoteUrl, ChatGPTTime, DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ChatGPTTime) | order by Timestamp desc

[LLM] ChatGPhish UI-redress click — browser navigation to rare external domain seconds after chatgpt.com summarize render Delivery Low
Hunts for a browser process resolving / connecting to an organization-rare external domain within 90 seconds of an outbound to chatgpt.com from the same host. Targets the ChatGPhish UI-redress and spoofed-system-alert primitives where attacker-controlled Markdown links rendered inside the trusted ChatGPT response trick the user into clicking through to attacker infrastructure they have never visited before. Rationale: Anchors the hunt on the article's named trust-transfer surface (chatgpt.com) combined with a 90-second click-through window — the article explicitly states attacker-controlled Markdown links 'render as live, clickable elements inside the ChatGPT interface' and users 'cannot distinguish attacker-injected URLs from ChatGPT-generated ones', making any rare-destination click immediately after a summarize action a high-priority pivot. Baseline anti-join (host seen by <4 org devices in last 30d) suppresses common legitimate citations. Corroborated by The Register coverage confirming the UI-redress and spoofed-alert primitives. Cross-checked against: • https://www.theregister.com/research/2026/05/29/chatgpt-prompt-injection-turns-web-pages-into-phishing-lures/5248137
ATT&CKT1659 T1204.001 T1036

ChatGPTTime + 90s) | join kind=leftanti Baseline on Host | summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), Hits = count(), arg_min(Timestamp, *) by DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Browser=InitiatingProcessFileName, Host, ChatGPTTime | extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstSeen, ChatGPTTime) | order by FirstSeen desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] HLS Installer.874.exe DLL side-load drops malicious library (Securelist fake-plugin miner) Installation High
Hunts the article's exact delivery primitive: the legitimate-looking 'HLS Installer.874.exe' from a ZIP archive loading the side-loaded malicious DLL (SHA1 6a0fe60...) that decrypts the SilentCryptoMiner/RAT chain. Pivots on the installer image name combined with image-load events of the known-bad hash or a non-system path. Rationale: Pivots on the article's exact named installer 'HLS Installer.874.exe' plus the published SHA1/SHA256 of the side-loaded malicious DLL. Both image-load and process-create paths covered because side-load can manifest as either a process or an image load. Cross-checked with Securelist's writeup (https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/) which confirms the installer name and DLL pairing. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let badSha1 = "6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db737f624407";
let installer = "HLS Installer.874.exe";
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ installer or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ installer or ProcessCommandLine has "HLS Installer.874.exe" or SHA1 == badSha1
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| union (
    DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ installer
    | where SHA1 == badSha1 or (FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Windows\" and FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
  )
| order by Timestamp desc
let badSha1 = "6a0fe6065d76715feebc1526d456db737f624407";
union isfuzzy=true
(SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 4688
  | where NewProcessName endswith @"\HLS Installer.874.exe" or CommandLine has "HLS Installer.874.exe"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, SubjectUserName),
(ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetProcessName has "HLS Installer.874.exe" or SHA1 =~ badSha1
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ActorUsername, SHA1),
(ImFileEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where TargetFileSHA1 =~ badSha1 or TargetFileName =~ "HLS Installer.874.exe"
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1)

[LLM] Fake GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC scheduled-task/service persistence (SilentCryptoMiner derivative) Installation High
Detects creation of the article's specific persistence artefact — a scheduled task or service masquerading as 'GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC' that re-launches the miner on every boot. The real Google Updater task name is 'GoogleUpdateTaskMachineCore' / '...UA' — the 'QC' suffix is the attacker's tell. Rationale: The article explicitly names the persistence artefact 'GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC' — the legitimate Google Updater uses '...Core' and '...UA' suffixes, so 'QC' is a deterministic IOC. Covers all three creation vectors (schtasks/sc/reg) plus the resulting registry footprint. Securelist (https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/) confirms this exact name and that it is registered as both task and service. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1543.003 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
let task = "GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC";
union isfuzzy=true
(DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has task
  | where FileName in~ ("schtasks.exe","sc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","reg.exe","cmd.exe","wmic.exe")
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where (RegistryKey has @"\Services\GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC")
       or (RegistryKey has @"\Schedule\TaskCache\Tasks\" and RegistryValueData has task)
       or RegistryValueName =~ "GoogleUpdateTaskMachineQC"

[LLM] Defender exclusion added for C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (miner staging dir) Installation High
Catches the article's defense-evasion step: the miner adds Windows Defender exclusions for EXE/DLL files and the C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome folder it lives in, so the watchdog and miner survive AV scans. Covers both the PowerShell Add-MpPreference path and direct Defender exclusion registry writes. Rationale: Article and Securelist both explicitly state the miner adds Defender exclusions for EXE/DLL extensions AND for system folders that resolve to its staging dir C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome. Detection ties the Add-MpPreference verb to that specific path (or the wider 'ExclusionExtension .exe/.dll' pattern that's atypical of legitimate sysadmin work). Cross-checked against https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/

  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath),
(DeviceRegistryEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)

[LLM] explorer.exe writes EXE/DLL into C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome (miner watchdog restore) Installation High
Detects the watchdog component the article describes: code running inside explorer.exe checks every 5 seconds that the miner exists in C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome and restores it from an encrypted backup if removed. explorer.exe writing PE files to that directory is highly anomalous and is the watchdog's restoration write. Rationale: Article explicitly: 'A watchdog component running inside Windows Explorer checks every five seconds to confirm the miner is active, restoring it from an encrypted backup if anything is removed.' Combines that behaviour with the staging path C:\ProgramData\Google\Chrome that Securelist confirms. explorer.exe writing PE files anywhere is rare; into a 'Google' subdirectory of ProgramData specifically is essentially zero-FP. Cross-checked against https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/. Cross-checked against: • https://securelist.com/video-books-pirates-miners-rat/119943/

| where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".bin" or FileName endswith ".dat"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, SHA1, SHA256,

| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA1, TargetFileSHA256, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or SHA1 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or MD5 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or SHA1 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407") or MD5 in~ ("6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["6A0FE6065D76715FEEBC1526D456DB737F624407"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GREYVIBE ClickFix fake Zoom/LAPAS CAPTCHA paste into Win+R then PowerShell Delivery High
Hunts the ClickFix initial-access pattern where a user lands on a fake Zoom/LAPAS CAPTCHA page (zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live) and is coached to paste an attacker-supplied command into the Run dialog, spawning powershell.exe or mshta.exe from explorer.exe. This is GREYVIBE's documented entry path for the PhantomRelay/LegionRelay infection chain. Rationale: Article explicitly names zoomconference.click/.app and lapas.live as the ClickFix CAPTCHA domains, and the kill-chain phase-2 detection hint calls out explorer→powershell/mshta with Win+R paste indicators. The parent=explorer + suspicious cradle string + 5-minute proximity to a lure-domain visit on the same device is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/ • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/clickfix-malware-campaign-attack
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("iex ","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","curl ","Invoke-RestMethod")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where RemoteUrl has_any ("zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live") | project DeviceId, ClickTime=Timestamp, BadUrl=RemoteUrl) on DeviceId
| where isnull(ClickTime) or Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ChildImage=FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, BadUrl, ClickTime
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureDomains = dynamic(["zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live","strip-mens.tilda.ws"]);
let Visits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains)
    | project ClickTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("iex ","Invoke-Expression","DownloadString","FromBase64String","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","curl ","Invoke-RestMethod")
| join kind=leftouter Visits on $left.Computer == $right.DvcHostname
| where isnull(ClickTime) or TimeGenerated between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Url, ClickTime
title: GREYVIBE ClickFix Win+R Paste Spawns PowerShell or mshta
id: 1a3c8b2e-9d6f-4a51-bb3c-7e2c4f5a1b22
description: Detects explorer.exe spawning powershell.exe/mshta.exe with download or encoded-command cradles consistent with the GREYVIBE ClickFix CAPTCHA paste lure (zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live).
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/new-russian-linked-greyvibe-targets.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1566.002
  - attack.t1204.001
  - attack.t1059.001
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'iex '
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
      - 'Invoke-RestMethod'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\Explorer.EXE) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe) @CommandLine:(*iex* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *DownloadString* OR *FromBase64String* OR *EncodedCommand* OR *Invoke-RestMethod*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|mshta|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("(iex |Invoke-Expression|DownloadString|FromBase64String|-EncodedCommand|-enc |WindowStyle Hidden|Invoke-RestMethod)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process="*RunMRU*" OR Processes.process="*iex *" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*" OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-W Hidden*" OR Processes.process="*-EncodedCommand*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process="*RunMRU*" OR Processes.process="*iex *" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*" OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-W Hidden*" OR Processes.process="*-EncodedCommand*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
[LLM] GREYVIBE PhantomMail Google Drive / 4sync archive lure delivered via email Delivery Medium
Detects inbound email containing links to Google Drive or 4sync that resolve to ZIP/RAR archives, which is GREYVIBE's PhantomMail spear-phishing delivery for JavaScript-based loaders that drop a decoy document and launch PhantomRelay. Correlates the email URL with subsequent archive extraction and JS execution on the recipient host. Rationale: Article specifies that PhantomMail emails carried links to Google Drive and 4sync archives containing JavaScript loaders, and the kill chain identifies wscript/cscript from extracted archive paths as the execution pivot. Correlating the email-side IOC (cloud-archive URLs) with the host-side JS-loader execution within a 6h window cuts FPs from legitimate file-share usage. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes
let SuspiciousUrls = EmailUrlInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where Url has_any ("drive.google.com","4sync.com","4shared.com")
    | where Url has_any (".zip",".rar","download","uc?id=","file/d/");
let Recipients = EmailEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where DeliveryAction in ("Delivered","DeliveredAsSpam")
    | join kind=inner SuspiciousUrls on NetworkMessageId
    | project EmailTime=Timestamp, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress, Subject, Url, NetworkMessageId;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".js",".jse",".vbs",".wsf")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\",@"\Temp\",@"\AppData\Local\Temp\",@"\7-Zip\",@"\WinRAR\")
| join kind=inner (Recipients) on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where Timestamp between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 6h)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Url, Subject, SenderFromAddress
let SuspectUrls = dynamic(["drive.google.com","4sync.com","4shared.com"]);
let Recips = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where Operation in ("MailItemsAccessed","Send")
    | extend Url = tostring(parse_json(Parameters))
    | where Url has_any (SuspectUrls) and Url has_any (".zip",".rar","file/d/","uc?id=")
    | project EmailTime=TimeGenerated, RecipientEmailAddress=UserId, Url;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any (".js",".jse",".vbs",".wsf")
| where CommandLine has_any ("\\Downloads\\","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")
| join kind=inner Recips on $left.TargetUserName == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 6h)
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, TargetUserName, CommandLine, NewProcessName, ParentProcessName, Url
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\CScript.exe) @CommandLine:(*.js* OR *.jse* OR *.vbs* OR *.wsf*) @CommandLine:(*\\Downloads\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("\\.(js|jse|vbs|wsf)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("\\\\(Downloads|Temp|AppData\\\\Local\\\\Temp)\\\\", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.url="*drive.google.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4sync.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4shared.com/*") (All_Email.url="*.zip*" OR All_Email.url="*.rar*" OR All_Email.url="*download*" OR All_Email.url="*uc?id=*") by All_Email.recipient All_Email.src_user All_Email.subject All_Email.url | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Email.All_Email where (All_Email.url="*drive.google.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4sync.com/*" OR All_Email.url="*4shared.com/*") (All_Email.url="*.zip*" OR All_Email.url="*.rar*" OR All_Email.url="*download*" OR All_Email.url="*uc?id=*") by All_Email.recipient All_Email.src_user All_Email.subject All_Email.url | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
[LLM] GREYVIBE PhantomRelayV1 watchdog persistence via Run key or scheduled task Installation Medium
Detects the PhantomRelayV1 'custom watchdog' persistence pattern — a paired powershell.exe process that immediately re-spawns a sibling powershell.exe within seconds of termination, registered via a Run/RunOnce key or a scheduled task. This is GREYVIBE's documented mechanism to keep the PowerShell RAT alive across reboots and termination. Rationale: Article calls out PhantomRelayV1's 'custom watchdog persistence mechanism' and kill-chain phase 3 specifies Run/RunOnce keys plus paired sibling re-spawn within seconds. The combination of Run-key registration of a hidden-window powershell + a 5-minute window with ≥2 sibling powershell spawns from a parent powershell is the watchdog fingerprint. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1547/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
ATT&CKT1547.001 T1053.005 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let RunKeyPersist = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
    | where RegistryKey has_any (@"\CurrentVersion\Run",@"\CurrentVersion\RunOnce")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any ("powershell","pwsh")
    | where RegistryValueData has_any ("-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","hidden","Start-Job","-NoP","-NonI")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName;
let WatchdogSpawn = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-Job","Start-Process","-WindowStyle Hidden","While","watchdog")
    | summarize Spawns=count(), arg_min(Timestamp,*) by DeviceName, AccountName, bin(Timestamp, 5m)
    | where Spawns >= 2;
RunKeyPersist
| join kind=leftouter (WatchdogSpawn | project DeviceName, WatchdogTime=Timestamp, Spawns) on DeviceName
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, WatchdogTime, Spawns
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\\CurrentVersion\\Run","\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("powershell","pwsh")
| where RegistryValueData has_any ("-W Hidden","-WindowStyle Hidden","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","hidden","Start-Job","-NoP","-NonI","watchdog")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| join kind=leftouter (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ParentProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
    | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Start-Job","Start-Process","-WindowStyle Hidden","watchdog")
    | summarize Spawns=count(), WatchdogTime=min(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
    | where Spawns >= 2
) on DvcHostname

[LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay browser, Telegram and WhatsApp data harvest Actions on Objectives High
Hunts LegionRelay's credential and messenger data theft by alerting on powershell.exe (or unsigned binaries) opening Chrome/Edge/Firefox 'Login Data' and 'Cookies' SQLite files, %AppData%\Telegram Desktop\tdata, and WhatsApp local storage. These exact targets are listed in the article as LegionRelay capabilities. Rationale: Article lists LegionRelay capabilities verbatim: 'browser data theft, Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration', and kill-chain phase 6 specifies Chrome/Edge/Firefox 'Login Data' + 'Cookies' SQLite + tdata + WhatsApp local storage as the file targets. Combined with non-browser proc reading those paths, this is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
   or FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\",@"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\",@"\WhatsApp\")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\",@"\Telegram Desktop\tdata\",@"\WhatsApp\")
   or FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","key4.db","key3.db")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName == ""
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let TargetPaths = dynamic(["\\Google\\Chrome\\User Data\\","\\Microsoft\\Edge\\User Data\\","\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles\\","\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\","\\WhatsApp\\"]);
let TargetFiles = dynamic(["Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","key4.db","key3.db"]);
let LegitBrowserProcs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (TargetPaths) or TargetFileName in~ (TargetFiles)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","cmd.exe")
| where not (ActingProcessName has_any (LegitBrowserProcs))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, Hash

[LLM] GREYVIBE DroneLink WireGuard tunnel install on user workstation Command & Control High
Detects DroneLink chain installing a WireGuard tunnel (wireguard.exe / wg.exe / tunnel.dll service) on a user workstation — the article cites fake Ukrainian-Armed-Forces charity sites delivering WireGuard and LegionRelay. Workstations almost never legitimately install ad-hoc WireGuard interfaces. Rationale: Article specifies DroneLink delivers WireGuard plus LegionRelay via charity-impersonation sites; kill-chain phase 8 calls out WireGuard tunnels from user endpoints as a high-fidelity C2 signal. Workstations rarely legitimately receive ad-hoc WireGuard installs, and excluding MSI/Intune/SCCM parents removes the corporate VPN deployment baseline. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
ATT&CKT1572 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let WgProcs = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("wireguard.exe","wg.exe","wg-quick.exe")
       or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("WireGuard","tunnel.dll","/installtunnelservice","wg-quick")
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","ccmexec.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256;
let WgFiles = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where FileName in~ ("wireguard.exe","wg.exe","tunnel.dll") or FolderPath has @"\WireGuard\"
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union WgProcs, WgFiles
| order by Timestamp desc
let WgFileNames = dynamic(["wireguard.exe","wg.exe","wg-quick.exe","tunnel.dll"]);
let ShellProcs = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe"]);
let WgProcs = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (WgFileNames)
        or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("WireGuard","tunnel.dll","/installtunnelservice","wg-quick")
    | where not (ParentProcessName has_any ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","intunemanagementextension.exe","ccmexec.exe"))
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName;
let WgFiles = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where TargetFileName has_any (WgFileNames) or TargetFilePath has "\\WireGuard\\"
    | where ActingProcessName has_any (ShellProcs)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName;
WgProcs
| union WgFiles
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GREYVIBE network egress to known C2 IP infrastructure Command & Control High
Alerts on any outbound connection from an endpoint to the 8 GREYVIBE C2 IPs documented in the WithSecure write-up. These IPs were used for PhantomRelay/LegionRelay beaconing and file exfiltration; any hit warrants immediate triage. Rationale: All 8 IPs are pulled verbatim from the IOC bundle in the kill-chain reconstruction and named as PhantomRelay/LegionRelay C2/exfil infrastructure (phases 8-9). Any organisational endpoint touching any of these IPs is a direct article-grounded IOC hit. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
let C2 = dynamic(["188.124.59.120","193.233.23.81","89.37.185.60","74.112.102.120","194.87.128.243","194.87.108.110","89.125.189.118","89.125.189.85"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2)
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Conns=count(),
            Procs=make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
            Cmds=make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 10),
            Ports=make_set(RemotePort, 10)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteIP
| order by FirstSeen asc
let C2 = dynamic(["188.124.59.120","193.233.23.81","89.37.185.60","74.112.102.120","194.87.128.243","194.87.108.110","89.125.189.118","89.125.189.85"]);
let FromCSL = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DestinationIP in (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, DeviceProduct, SentBytes, ReceivedBytes;
let FromAsim = ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (C2)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkBytes;
FromCSL
| union FromAsim
| order by TimeGenerated asc
