[LLM] GREYVIBE LegionRelay RDP enablement and outbound 3389 from user endpoint Command & Control High
Detects LegionRelay's RDP-access-setup behaviour: registry change enabling Terminal Services (fDenyTSConnections=0) and/or firewall rule allowing RDP, followed by outbound TCP/3389 from a workstation that normally does not initiate RDP. Article explicitly lists 'RDP access setup' as a LegionRelay capability. Rationale: Article calls out 'RDP access setup' as a LegionRelay capability; the standard mechanism is flipping fDenyTSConnections=0 plus a firewall allow rule. Pairing the registry change with a netsh/PowerShell firewall command in the same hour, on a workstation, is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1112 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let RdpEnable = DeviceRegistryEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (RegistryKey has @"\Terminal Server" and RegistryValueName =~ "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0")
         or (RegistryKey has @"\WinStations\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValueName =~ "UserAuthentication")
    | project RegTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
let FwRule = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where (FileName =~ "netsh.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "Remote Desktop")
         or (FileName =~ "powershell.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-NetFirewallRule -DisplayGroup \"Remote Desktop\"","Enable-NetFirewallRule"))
    | project FwTime=Timestamp, DeviceName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName;
RdpEnable
| join kind=leftouter FwRule on DeviceName
| where isnull(FwTime) or FwTime between (RegTime - 1h .. RegTime + 1h)
| project RegTime, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FwTime, FwCmd=ProcessCommandLine
let RdpEnable = ImRegistryEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (RegistryKey has "\\Terminal Server" and RegistryValue =~ "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0")
         or (RegistryKey has "\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValue =~ "UserAuthentication")
    | project RegTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine;
let FwRule = ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where (ActingProcessName has "netsh.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "Remote Desktop")
         or (ActingProcessName has "powershell.exe" and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Set-NetFirewallRule","Enable-NetFirewallRule"))
    | project FwTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessCommandLine;
RdpEnable
| join kind=leftouter FwRule on DvcHostname
| where isnull(FwTime) or FwTime between (RegTime - 1h .. RegTime + 1h)

[LLM] GREYVIBE princess-club and Zoom/LAPAS lookalike domain access Reconnaissance High
Hunts inbound or outbound web traffic to the lure domains GREYVIBE used across PhantomClick, PrincessClub and Nebo: zoomconference.click/.app, lapas.live, strip-mens.tilda.ws, princess-mens.fun/.click/.com, princessclub.click. Captures both the initial-access click and any WebRTC AV-capture follow-on. Rationale: Article and IOC bundle name every one of these domains as lures used in PhantomClick (Zoom/LAPAS), PrincessClub (princess-* / strip-mens) and related chains. Any organisational endpoint resolving or visiting these is a direct article-grounded IOC hit; resolution covers the WebRTC-AV-capture flow as well. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/002/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001 T1204.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
let LureDomains = dynamic(["zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live","strip-mens.tilda.ws","princess-mens.fun","princess-mens-club.com","princess-mens.click","princessclub.click"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (LureDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP;
let UrlHits = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains)
    | project Timestamp, AccountUpn, Url, ActionType, IPAddress, IsClickedThrough;
NetHits
| union (UrlHits | extend DeviceName="<email-click>", InitiatingProcessAccountName=AccountUpn, RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP=IPAddress)
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureDomains = dynamic(["zoomconference.click","zoomconference.app","lapas.live","strip-mens.tilda.ws","princess-mens.fun","princess-mens-club.com","princess-mens.click","princessclub.click"]);
let WebHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where Url has_any (LureDomains) or HttpHostName has_any (LureDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpHostName;
let DnsHits = ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery has_any (LureDomains)
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DnsQuery;
WebHits
| union DnsHits
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GREYVIBE XMRig miner deployment on LegionRelay-infected host Actions on Objectives High
Detects XMRig command-line invocation (stratum+tcp, --donate-level, -o, --tls-fingerprint) on an endpoint, which the article notes GREYVIBE deploys on a subset of LegionRelay-infected machines for monetisation alongside espionage. The combination of mining-pool C2 strings on a normally-non-mining host is high-fidelity. Rationale: Article phase-10 detection hint specifies XMRig command-line flags (-o, --donate-level, stratum+tcp) and mining pool connections. These strings are mining-specific and almost never appear in legitimate enterprise software on a user workstation. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://github.com/xmrig/xmrig
ATT&CKT1496
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp","stratum+ssl","--donate-level","--randomx","-o pool.","--tls-fingerprint","xmrig")
   or FileName =~ "xmrig.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp","stratum+ssl","--donate-level","--randomx","-o pool.","--tls-fingerprint","xmrig")
   or ActingProcessName =~ "xmrig.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"

        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hackers Use Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages to Deliver ScreenConnect Malware

Cyber Security News
2026-05-29 13 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A sophisticated phishing campaign is actively targeting financial organizations by using fake Adobe Document Cloud pages to silently install ScreenConnect remote access malware on victim machines. The operation is well-structured, deceptive, and difficult to detect because it blends into everyday enterprise software activity. The campaign works by sending phishing emails that look like legitimate Adobe [&#8230;] The post Hackers Use Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages to Deliver ScreenConnect Malware appeared first on Cyber Security News .

ATT&CKT1021.001 T1027 T1190 T1219 T1566 T1566.001

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] RatPressto phishing-kit URL paths on compromised WordPress hosts (/download.html, /complete.php, /download.php) · [LLM] Browser/email-client drop of ScreenConnect installer or victim-named VBS dropper (RatPressto silent download) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hackers Use Fake Adobe Document Cloud Pages to Deliver ScreenConnect Malware
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] ScreenConnect MSI install via msiexec from user-writable temp/Downloads (RatPressto delivery) · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] ScreenConnect agent beaconing to RatPressto C2 (TCP/8041 to zistopstoabetterlife.com / 177.154.191.148 / 84.32.41.64) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] RatPressto phishing-kit URL paths on compromised WordPress hosts (/download.html, /complete.php, /download.php) Delivery High
Hunts browser hits to the RatPressto stage-1/stage-2 URI paths on the specific compromised/actor-controlled WordPress domains named by Fortra FIRE. The path triplet (download.html → complete.php → download.php) plus the IOC domain set is the cleanest article-specific lure fingerprint. Rationale: Article explicitly names download.html / complete.php / download.php as the kit's three deployment files (stage-1, stage-2, hidden iframe) on the listed compromised WordPress hosts. Combining the path triplet with the IOC domain set yields a near-zero-FP fingerprint.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1189

title: RatPressto Fake Adobe Phishing Kit URL Paths
id: 7a2f3b1c-4d8e-4f60-9c1a-5e8b9a2d1f01
description: Detects browser/proxy hits to the RatPressto phishing kit stage paths (/download.html, /complete.php, /download.php) on Fortra-FIRE-named compromised WordPress hosts that deliver ScreenConnect installers.
references:
  - https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-use-fake-adobe-document-cloud-pages/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1566.002
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection_path:
    cs-uri-stem|endswith:
      - '/download.html'
      - '/complete.php'
      - '/download.php'
  selection_host:
    cs-host|contains:
      - 'zistopstoabetterlife'
      - 'ampliawifi.com'
      - 'gaheempreendimentos.com'
      - 'iconclinic.ae'
      - 'kinorot.co.il'
      - 'vetcarebd.xyz'
      - 'nabellacouture.com'
      - 'birexo.icu'
      - 'abpmed.com'
  condition: selection_path and selection_host
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR proxy OR zscaler) (@http.url:(*/download.html OR */complete.php OR */download.php) OR @url:(*/download.html OR */complete.php OR */download.php)) AND (@http.url_details.host:(zistopstoabetterlife.com OR ampliawifi.com OR gaheempreendimentos.com OR iconclinic.ae OR kinorot.co.il OR vetcarebd.xyz OR nabellacouture.com OR birexo.icu OR abpmed.com) OR @network.destination.name:(zistopstoabetterlife.com OR ampliawifi.com OR gaheempreendimentos.com OR iconclinic.ae OR kinorot.co.il OR vetcarebd.xyz OR nabellacouture.com OR birexo.icu OR abpmed.com))
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(zistopstoabetterlife|ampliawifi|gaheempreendimentos|iconclinic|kinorot|vetcarebd|nabellacouture|birexo|abpmed)/i
| join(query={#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemotePort=443}, field=[aid], include=[RemoteAddressIP4,ContextImageFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, DomainName, ContextImageFileName], function=count())

[LLM] ScreenConnect MSI install via msiexec from user-writable temp/Downloads (RatPressto delivery) Installation High
Catches the RatPressto execution stage: msiexec launched against a ScreenConnect installer staged in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, including the victim-renamed variants observed (ceo.msi, microsoftceo.exe, ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.msi). Pivots specifically on path + filename rather than generic msiexec usage. Rationale: Article names msiexec from temp directories as the documented infection-chain pivot and lists ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.msi, ceo.msi, microsoftceo.exe, and CapraAssetManagementInc.vbs as the specific dropper artefacts. Tying msiexec to those exact strings keeps FPs near zero versus a generic 'msiexec from temp' hunt.
ATT&CKT1218.007 T1204.002 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "msiexec.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("ScreenConnect.ClientSetup", "ceo.msi", "microsoftceo", "CapraAssetManagement")
   or (ProcessCommandLine has ".msi" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Temp", "Downloads", "AppData\\Local", "AppData\\Roaming"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sccm.exe","ccmexec.exe","msiexec.exe","trustedinstaller.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "msiexec.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("ScreenConnect.ClientSetup", "ceo.msi", "microsoftceo", "CapraAssetManagement")
   or (CommandLine has ".msi" and CommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\", "\\Downloads\\", "\\AppData\\"))
| where ParentProcessName !endswith "ccmexec.exe" and ParentProcessName !endswith "TrustedInstaller.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] ScreenConnect agent beaconing to RatPressto C2 (TCP/8041 to zistopstoabetterlife.com / 177.154.191.148 / 84.32.41.64) Command & Control High
High-confidence C2 detection on the self-hosted ScreenConnect relay called out in the article: TCP/8041 to *.zistopstoabetterlife.com, the São Paulo IP 177.154.191.148, or 84.32.41.64. Catches both the install-time relay arg and the steady-state agent heartbeat. Rationale: Article explicitly states the C2 is cloud.zistopstoabetterlife.com on TCP/8041 with São Paulo hosting at 177.154.191.148 and an associated 84.32.41.64. Three IOCs + non-standard port make this a high-confidence alert with negligible FP risk.
ATT&CKT1219 T1571 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (RemotePort == 8041 and RemoteIPType == "Public")
   or RemoteUrl has "zistopstoabetterlife.com"
   or RemoteIP in ("177.154.191.148", "84.32.41.64")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (DstPortNumber == 8041 and DstIpAddr !startswith "10." and DstIpAddr !startswith "192.168." and DstIpAddr !startswith "172.")
   or DstHostname has "zistopstoabetterlife.com"
   or DstIpAddr in ("177.154.191.148", "84.32.41.64")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstHostname, DstPortNumber, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Browser/email-client drop of ScreenConnect installer or victim-named VBS dropper (RatPressto silent download) Delivery Medium
Detects the hidden-iframe download stage: browsers or Outlook writing a ScreenConnect MSI, microsoftceo.exe, ceo.msi, or a company-name-prefixed .vbs into Downloads/Temp/AppData. Catches the kit's victim-customised filenames (e.g. CapraAssetManagementInc.vbs). Rationale: Article calls out that the iframe silently drops ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.msi and that file names are customised to match the victim's business context (microsoftceo.exe, ceo.msi, CapraAssetManagementInc.vbs are explicit examples). Watching for browser/email writes of these exact names — or a company-name-style VBS — directly fingerprints the kit.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where (FileName in~ ("ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.msi", "microsoftceo.exe", "ceo.msi", "CapraAssetManagementInc.vbs"))
   or (FileName endswith ".vbs" and FileName matches regex @"^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{4,}(Inc|LLC|Ltd|Corp|Group|Holdings|Capital|Partners|Asset[A-Za-z]*)\.vbs$")
   or (FileName endswith ".msi" and FileName has_any ("ScreenConnect", "ClientSetup"))
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","outlook.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any ("Downloads", "AppData\\Local\\Temp", "AppData\\Roaming", "AppData\\Local\\Microsoft\\Windows\\INetCache")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileOriginUrl, FileOriginReferrerUrl, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where (TargetFileName in~ ("ScreenConnect.ClientSetup.msi", "microsoftceo.exe", "ceo.msi", "CapraAssetManagementInc.vbs"))
   or (TargetFileName endswith ".vbs" and TargetFileName matches regex @"^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]{4,}(Inc|LLC|Ltd|Corp|Group|Holdings|Capital|Partners|Asset[A-Za-z]*)\.vbs$")
   or (TargetFileName endswith ".msi" and TargetFileName has_any ("ScreenConnect", "ClientSetup"))
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","iexplore.exe","outlook.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("Downloads", "AppData\\Local\\Temp", "AppData\\Roaming")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

        where DNS.query IN ("cloud.zistopstoabetterlife.com", "zistopstoabetterlife.com", "ampliawifi.com", "gaheempreendimentos.com", "c3po3090.com.br", "iconclinic.ae", "kinorot.co.il", "vetcarebd.xyz", "nabellacouture.com", "birexo.icu")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Steals OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens

Cyber Security News
2026-05-29 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

A polished, fully functional npm package has been caught secretly stealing OpenAI Codex authentication tokens from developers who trusted it. The package, named codexui-android, presented itself as a remote web UI for OpenAI Codex with no obvious signs of being malicious. It built a genuine user base, amassed 27,000 weekly downloads, and maintained an active [&#8230;] The post Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Steals OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens appeared first on Cyber Security News .

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Article-specific behavioural hunt — Legitimate-Looking Codex Remote UI Steals OpenAI Codex Authentication Tokens
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] codexui-android npm package install or chunk-PUR7OUAG.js write on developer host · [LLM] Android emulator / WSL extracts Linux rootfs and runs node.exe pulling unpinned npm
Command & Control. [LLM] HTTP POST to /startlog with XOR+base64 stealer beacon shape Command & Control High
Detects the specific HTTP POST shape used by the codexui-android stealer: a POST to a URL ending in /startlog on the anyclaw.store infrastructure (or any host) carrying a base64-encoded XOR("anyclaw2026") body. Catches actor infrastructure pivots where they reuse the same path but rotate the domain. Rationale: Article + IOC table specify POST /startlog as the exfil endpoint. Pairing the path with codexui-android-typical parents (node, npm, electron, java for the Android app) lowers FP risk vs path-only matching. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/legitimate-looking-codex-remote-ui/

[LLM] Codex auth.json read followed by outbound HTTP within 60s (token theft pattern) Actions on Objectives Medium
Temporal correlation: a node.exe or related JS runtime reads the user's Codex auth.json credential file, then within 60 seconds initiates an outbound HTTPS POST. Matches the codexui-android stealer's exact behaviour of loading at module init, reading auth.json, XOR+base64 encoding, and posting to the C2 — without needing the C2 domain itself, so survives infra rotation. Rationale: Article states the malicious code 'fired the moment the tool launched' and 'targeted the auth.json file stored at the user's Codex home directory' then sent contents to attacker server. The auth.json + same-process outbound POST within 60s captures the behaviour even if the C2 domain changes. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/legitimate-looking-codex-remote-ui/

  | project ReadTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AuthFolderPath=FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;

  | project NetTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort;

| order by ReadTime desc

[LLM] Android emulator / WSL extracts Linux rootfs and runs node.exe pulling unpinned npm Installation Medium
Detects the codexui-android Android app's distinctive on-host execution chain: an Android emulator or WSL process extracts rootfs.tar.zst.bin into private storage, then spawns node.exe which runs `npm install codexui-android` (or similar) with no version pin, pulling whatever the current malicious build is at runtime. This is the second-stage delivery vector described for the 'OpenClaw Codex Claude AI Agent' app. Rationale: Article details the Android app extracts a Linux env, runs Node.js, and installs the malicious npm package 'without pinning a version'. rootfs.tar.zst.bin is the named userland archive; gptos.intelligence.assistant and codex.app are the named Play Store package IDs; app.anyclaw.* is the shared Kotlin namespace — all from the IOC table. Cross-checked against: • https://cybersecuritynews.com/legitimate-looking-codex-remote-ui/
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1195.002 T1027.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceFileEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "rootfs.tar.zst.bin" or FileName endswith ".tar.zst.bin"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, EventKind="rootfs-drop"),
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "node.exe" or FileName =~ "npm.exe" or FileName =~ "npx.exe"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android"
     or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "app.anyclaw"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "gptos.intelligence.assistant"
     or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "codex.app"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, EventKind="node-pulls-codexui")
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
( DeviceFileEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "rootfs.tar.zst.bin"
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DeviceName, User=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Process=InitiatingProcessFileName, Cmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, EventKind="rootfs-drop"),
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.exe","npx.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "codexui-android" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("gptos.intelligence.assistant","codex.app","app.anyclaw")
  | project TimeGenerated, Host=DeviceName, User=AccountName, Process=InitiatingProcessFileName, Cmd=ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, EventKind="node-pulls-codexui"),
( ImProcessCreate

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Sicoob.Sdk malicious NuGet package present on developer host (v2.0.0–2.0.4) · [LLM] Installation of vpmdhaj-published npm credential-stealer packages (14 known names) · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm install lifecycle script reads AWS/Vault/CI credentials within minutes of package install · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Outbound HTTPS or DNS to Sicoob/npm-cluster exfil domains (aab.sportsontheweb.net, oob.moika.tech) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] PFX certificate read by .NET process followed by HTTPS egress to fake-Sentry domain · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Sicoob.Sdk malicious NuGet package present on developer host (v2.0.0–2.0.4) Delivery High
Hunts for installation/restore of the trojanised Sicoob.Sdk NuGet package on developer or build hosts. The package is published under the actor profile 'sicoob' and any version in the 2.0.0–2.0.4 range is malicious — its SicoobClient class reads PFX certs from disk and exfiltrates them to a hardcoded fake-Sentry endpoint. Rationale: Hits the article's most specific IOC — package name 'Sicoob.Sdk' restricted to the exact malicious version range 2.0.0–2.0.4 published by Socket. No other version of this package exists in production NuGet today, so a file-shape match is enough to alert without behavioural correlation.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where (FolderPath has @"\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or FolderPath has @"\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or FolderPath has @"/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/")
| extend pkgVersion = extract(@"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/](\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, FolderPath)
| where pkgVersion in ("2.0.0","2.0.1","2.0.2","2.0.3","2.0.4")
| where FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".nupkg" or FileName endswith ".nuspec"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, pkgVersion, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or TargetFilePath has @"\packages\sicoob.sdk\" or TargetFilePath has @"/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/"
| extend pkgVersion = extract(@"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/](\d+\.\d+\.\d+)", 1, TargetFilePath)
| where pkgVersion in ("2.0.0","2.0.1","2.0.2","2.0.3","2.0.4")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("dll","nupkg","nuspec")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, pkgVersion, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects file events under .nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk for the malicious 2.0.0-2.0.4 versions reported by Socket. Package exfiltrates PFX certs to aab.sportsontheweb.net.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/malicious-sicoob-nuget-steals-banking.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_path:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.0\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.1\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.2\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.3\'
      - '\.nuget\packages\sicoob.sdk\2.0.4\'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.dll'
      - '.nupkg'
      - '.nuspec'
  condition: selection_path and selection_ext
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:(*\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.0\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.1\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.2\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.3\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\2.0.4\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.0\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.1\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.2\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.3\\* OR *\\.nuget\\packages\\Sicoob.Sdk\\2.0.4\\*))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob\.sdk\\(2\.0\.[0-4])\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName], function=[count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | eval version=case(match(file_path,"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/]2\.0\.[0-4]"),"malicious-2.0.0-2.0.4",1=1,"other-check") | where version="malicious-2.0.0-2.0.4" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.nuget\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\packages\\sicoob.sdk\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.nuget/packages/sicoob.sdk/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | eval version=case(match(file_path,"(?i)sicoob\.sdk[\\/]2\.0\.[0-4]"),"malicious-2.0.0-2.0.4",1=1,"other-check") | where version="malicious-2.0.0-2.0.4" | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
[LLM] PFX certificate read by .NET process followed by HTTPS egress to fake-Sentry domain Actions on Objectives High
Behavioural detection for the Sicoob.Sdk exfil chain: SicoobClient opens a .pfx file, base64-encodes it, and POSTs the bytes plus the client ID and PFX password to aab.sportsontheweb.net (a Sentry-impersonating domain). Correlates a PFX file event with an outbound network event by the same .NET process within 5 minutes. Rationale: Combines two article-specific signals: PFX file access by a .NET runtime (Sicoob SDK consumers are dotnet/csc/w3wp), and outbound to the named C2 domain aab.sportsontheweb.net, plus the sibling C2 oob.moika.tech for the parallel npm cluster. Same-process+5-minute correlation makes this very low-noise.
ATT&CKT1552.004 T1041 T1102
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
let lookback = 30d;
let maxDelay = 5m;
let PfxReads = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName endswith ".pfx" or FileName endswith ".p12"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","MSBuild.exe")
| project PfxTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, PfxPath=FolderPath, PfxFile=FileName;
let Egress = DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech") or RemoteIP in ("")
| project NetTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort;
PfxReads
| join kind=inner Egress on DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId
| where NetTime between (PfxTime .. PfxTime + maxDelay)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, PfxTime)
| project PfxTime, NetTime, DelaySec, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, PfxPath, PfxFile, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| order by PfxTime desc
let lookback = 30d;
let maxDelay = 5m;
let PfxReads = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("pfx","p12")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","MSBuild.exe")
| project PfxTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername, PfxPath=TargetFilePath;
let Egress = ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where DstHostname has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech") or Url has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech")
| project NetTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId=tostring(SrcPortNumber), DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber;
PfxReads
| join kind=inner Egress on DvcHostname
| where NetTime between (PfxTime .. PfxTime + maxDelay)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', NetTime, PfxTime)
| project PfxTime, NetTime, DelaySec, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, PfxPath, DstHostname, DstIpAddr
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*.pfx OR *.p12 OR *.PFX OR *.P12) @Image:(*\\dotnet.exe OR *\\w3wp.exe OR *\\csc.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\Dotnet.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:(*sportsontheweb.net OR *moika.tech))
(#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten) TargetFileName=/\.(pfx|p12)$/i ContextImageFileName=/(dotnet|w3wp|csc|powershell|pwsh|MSBuild)\.exe$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ContextImageFileName=/(dotnet|w3wp|csc|powershell|pwsh|MSBuild)\.exe$/i | regex("(sportsontheweb\.net|moika\.tech)", field=RemoteAddressIP4) OR DomainName=/(sportsontheweb\.net|moika\.tech)$/i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[RemoteAddressIP4, DomainName, RemotePort])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, RemoteAddressIP4], function=count())
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as pfx_time from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.pfx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.p12") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as host, process_id as pid | join type=inner host pid [| tstats `summariesonly` min(_time) as net_time from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_host="*sportsontheweb.net" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*moika.tech") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_id All_Traffic.dest_host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | rename src as host, process_id as pid] | where net_time>=pfx_time AND (net_time-pfx_time)<=300 | eval delay_sec=net_time-pfx_time | table host user process_name pfx_time net_time delay_sec file_path dest_host
| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as pfx_time from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_name="*.pfx" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.p12") AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("dotnet.exe","w3wp.exe","csc.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_id Filesystem.file_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as host, process_id as pid | join type=inner host pid [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as net_time from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where (All_Traffic.dest_host="*sportsontheweb.net" OR All_Traffic.dest_host="*moika.tech") by All_Traffic.src All_Traffic.process_id All_Traffic.dest_host | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | rename src as host, process_id as pid] | where net_time>=pfx_time AND (net_time-pfx_time)<=300 | eval delay_sec=net_time-pfx_time | table host user process_name pfx_time net_time delay_sec file_path dest_host
[LLM] npm install lifecycle script reads AWS/Vault/CI credentials within minutes of package install Installation High
Hunts the 'vpmdhaj' preinstall-hook chain plus the broader npm credential-harvester pattern. Looks for a node/npm/yarn/pnpm process touching ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.vault-token, ~/.npmrc, .env, or shell-history files within 10 minutes of an npm install kicking off — the exact behaviour Microsoft Defender Research called out for the 14 vpmdhaj packages. Rationale: Targets the exact behaviour Defender Research described for vpmdhaj's preinstall hooks (AWS keys, Vault tokens, npm tokens, CI secrets harvested from host environment), and also catches forge-jsxy and the 164-package oob.moika.tech cluster which share the same pattern. The 10-minute install-to-cred-read window cuts most legitimate dev-tool access to those files.
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1059.007 T1546.016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where FileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," i "," ci "," add ") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallCmd=ProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where (FolderPath has @"\.aws\" or FolderPath has @"/.aws/"
      or FileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
      or FolderPath has @"\.vault" or FolderPath has @"/.vault"
      or FolderPath has @"\.docker\config" or FolderPath has @"/.docker/config"
      or FolderPath has @"\.kube\config" or FolderPath has @"/.kube/config")
| project CredTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, CredPath=FolderPath, CredFile=FileName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
Installs
| join kind=inner CredHits on DeviceId
| where CredTime between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + maxDelay)
| summarize CredFilesTouched=make_set(strcat(CredPath, CredFile), 25), FirstCred=min(CredTime), LastCred=max(CredTime), Cmd=any(InstallCmd) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InstallTime
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstCred, InstallTime)
| order by InstallTime desc
let lookback = 14d;
let maxDelay = 10m;
let Installs = ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.cmd","pnpm.exe","node.exe") or ParentProcessName has_any ("npm.cmd","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall"," ci "," add ") or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any (" install","preinstall","postinstall")
| project InstallTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, InstallCmd=ActingProcessCommandLine;
let CredHits = ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe","npm.exe","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe")
| where TargetFilePath has @"\.aws\" or TargetFilePath has @"/.aws/"
     or TargetFileName in~ (".vault-token",".npmrc",".env",".bash_history",".zsh_history")
     or TargetFilePath has @".vault"
     or TargetFilePath has ".docker/config" or TargetFilePath has ".kube/config"
| project CredTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, CredPath=TargetFilePath;
Installs
| join kind=inner CredHits on DvcHostname
| where CredTime between (InstallTime .. InstallTime + maxDelay)
| summarize CredFilesTouched=make_set(CredPath, 25), FirstCred=min(CredTime), Cmd=any(InstallCmd) by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, InstallTime
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', FirstCred, InstallTime)
| order by InstallTime desc
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\npm.cmd OR *\\npm.exe OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe) @CommandLine:(*preinstall* OR *postinstall* OR *"npm install"* OR *"npm ci"*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.parent.name:(npm OR node OR yarn OR pnpm) (@process.command_line:*preinstall* OR @process.command_line:*install*)) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\npm.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\.aws\\credentials* OR *\\.vault-token* OR *\\.npmrc* OR *\\.env OR *.docker\\config* OR *.kube\\config*))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 OR #event_simpleName=SyntheticProcessRollup2) ImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i CommandLine=/(preinstall|postinstall|\sinstall\b|\sci\b|\sadd\b)/i
| join({#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo OR #event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(node|npm|yarn|pnpm)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i TargetFileName=/(\.aws[\\\/]credentials|\.vault-token|\.npmrc$|[\\\/]\.env$|\.bash_history|\.zsh_history|\.docker[\\\/]config|\.kube[\\\/]config)/i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[TargetFileName])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine], function=[count(), collect(TargetFileName)])
ENDPOINT

| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as install_time from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="npm.cmd" OR Processes.process_name="npm.exe" OR Processes.process_name="yarn.exe" OR Processes.process_name="pnpm.exe" OR Processes.process_name="node.exe") AND (Processes.process="*install*" OR Processes.process="*preinstall*" OR Processes.process="*postinstall*") by Processes.dest Processes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename dest as host | join type=inner host [| tstats summariesonly=false min(_time) as cred_time values(Filesystem.file_path) as cred_paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\.aws\\credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.vault-token*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.vault-token*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_name=".env" OR Filesystem.file_name=".bash_history" OR Filesystem.file_name=".zsh_history") AND (Filesystem.process_name="node.exe" OR Filesystem.process_name="node" OR Filesystem.process_name="npm.exe") by Filesystem.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | rename dest as host] | where cred_time>=install_time AND (cred_time-install_time)<=600 | eval delay_sec=cred_time-install_time | table host user install_time cred_time delay_sec cred_paths
[LLM] Outbound HTTPS or DNS to Sicoob/npm-cluster exfil domains (aab.sportsontheweb.net, oob.moika.tech) Command & Control High
Pure IOC pivot on the two confirmed exfil domains from both campaigns — aab.sportsontheweb.net is the Sicoob.Sdk fake-Sentry endpoint, oob.moika.tech is the 164-npm-package /report beacon. Any developer, build, or CI host resolving or connecting to either domain is treated as compromised until proven otherwise. Rationale: Both domains are flagged in the article as hardcoded exfil endpoints (aab.sportsontheweb.net for Sicoob.Sdk's fake-Sentry POSTs, oob.moika.tech/report for the 164-npm-package env-var beacon). Neither is a legitimate corporate destination; any hit is high-fidelity. Wildcards on parent domains catch subdomain rotation by the actor.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002 T1567.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("aab.sportsontheweb.net","sportsontheweb.net","oob.moika.tech","moika.tech")
| project Timestamp, Source="NetworkConnect", DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech")
| project Timestamp, Source="DnsQuery", DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP=tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IpAddress), RemotePort=int(0))
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstHostname has_any ("aab.sportsontheweb.net","sportsontheweb.net","oob.moika.tech","moika.tech") or Url has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech")
| project TimeGenerated, Source="NetworkSession", DvcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url),
(ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery has_any ("sportsontheweb.net","moika.tech")
| project TimeGenerated, Source="DnsQuery", DvcHostname, SrcUsername=SrcUsername, DstHostname=DnsQuery, DstIpAddr="", DstPortNumber=int(53), Url="")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Installation of vpmdhaj-published npm credential-stealer packages (14 known names) Delivery High
File-event hunt for any of the 14 npm packages published by 'vpmdhaj' (a39155771@gmail.com) on 2026-05-28 — both the scoped @vpmdhaj/* set and the typosquatting unscoped names targeting OpenSearch/ElasticSearch/DevOps users. Presence in any host's node_modules is sufficient to alert. Rationale: Direct IOC match on the 14 named packages from the article (both the @vpmdhaj/* scope and the 10 typosquatting unscoped names). Filters on package.json/index.js/preinstall.js/postinstall.js keep the alert to one event per install rather than firing for every file extracted from the tarball.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let MaliciousPaths = dynamic([
  @"\node_modules\@vpmdhaj\devops-tools\",
  @"\node_modules\@vpmdhaj\elastic-helper\",
  @"\node_modules\@vpmdhaj\opensearch-setup\",
  @"\node_modules\@vpmdhaj\search-setup\",
  @"\node_modules\app-config-utility\",
  @"\node_modules\elastic-opensearch-helper\",
  @"\node_modules\env-config-manager\",
  @"\node_modules\opensearch-config-utility\",
  @"\node_modules\opensearch-security-scanner\",
  @"\node_modules\opensearch-setup\",
  @"\node_modules\opensearch-setup-tool\",
  @"\node_modules\search-cluster-setup\",
  @"\node_modules\search-engine-setup\",
  @"\node_modules\vpmdhaj-opensearch-setup\",
  "/node_modules/@vpmdhaj/",
  "/node_modules/app-config-utility/",
  "/node_modules/elastic-opensearch-helper/",
  "/node_modules/env-config-manager/",
  "/node_modules/opensearch-config-utility/",
  "/node_modules/opensearch-security-scanner/",
  "/node_modules/opensearch-setup/",
  "/node_modules/opensearch-setup-tool/",
  "/node_modules/search-cluster-setup/",
  "/node_modules/search-engine-setup/",
  "/node_modules/vpmdhaj-opensearch-setup/"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has_any (MaliciousPaths)
| where FileName in~ ("package.json","index.js","preinstall.js","postinstall.js") or FileName endswith ".tgz"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let MaliciousPaths = dynamic([

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
