Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

| sort - click_time

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName

// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Exploitation. Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] GreyVibe: RDP enablement via fDenyTSConnections=0 + firewall by PowerShell RAT
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] PowerShell.exe sustained beaconing to uncategorized web endpoint (LegionRelay/PhantomRelay C2) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] LegionRelay browser credential theft from Chromium/Firefox Login Data by PowerShell · [LLM] LegionRelay Telegram / WhatsApp messenger store exfiltration · [LLM] GreyVibe cryptocurrency miner deployment via PowerShell RAT
[LLM] PhantomMail: Ukrainian-themed ZIP/RAR delivered via Google Drive or 4sync links Delivery Medium
Hunts GreyVibe's PhantomMail vector: spear-phishing emails with ZIP/RAR attachments or body links to Google Drive / 4sync, themed against Ukrainian gov, emergency, telecom or energy entities. Pivots on archive attachments plus the two specific cloud-storage URL families called out by WithSecure. Rationale: Anchors on WithSecure-stated PhantomMail strings: ZIP/RAR archives, Google Drive and 4sync links, and Ukrainian gov/emergency/telecom/energy lure impersonation. Mail-only signal so endpoint queries are deferred to the execution UCs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] PhantomClick: browser → mshta/powershell/cmd within 60s of fake Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS lure Exploitation High
Hunts the PhantomClick ClickFix flow: victim visits a fake Zoom or LAPAS site, the page displays a fake Cloudflare verification, and the user pastes a self-infecting command. Pivots on a browser parent spawning interpreter children within seconds, with the cmdline carrying ClickFix-style payload markers. Rationale: Maps directly to WithSecure's PhantomClick description: fake Cloudflare/Zoom/LAPAS verification leading users to paste self-infecting commands. Combines browser parent + interpreter child + ClickFix telltale strings (Cloudflare, ray-id, captcha, lapas, Verify you are human). Cross-checked against MITRE T1204.001 and recurring ClickFix Sigma rules to ensure novelty. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/

[LLM] LegionRelay browser credential theft from Chromium/Firefox Login Data by PowerShell Actions on Objectives High
Hunts LegionRelay's browser credential-theft module: PowerShell or other non-browser processes reading Chromium 'Login Data' / 'Local State' and Firefox 'logins.json' / 'key4.db'. Article calls out browser credential theft as a built-in capability of the LegionRelay RAT. Rationale: WithSecure says LegionRelay 'supports … browser credential theft'. Targets the universal artefact paths of the Chromium and Firefox credential vaults, gated on a non-browser scripting-host parent — the article calls out LegionRelay as a PowerShell-based RAT. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Local State","logins.json","key4.db","cookies.sqlite","Cookies","Web Data") | where FolderPath has_any ("\\Google\\Chrome\\","\\Microsoft\\Edge\\","\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\","\\BraveSoftware\\","\\Opera Software\\") | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","explorer.exe","searchprotocolhost.exe","backup.exe") | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe") | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType | order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Local State","logins.json","key4.db","cookies.sqlite","Cookies","Web Data") | where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\Google\\Chrome\\","\\Microsoft\\Edge\\","\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\","\\BraveSoftware\\","\\Opera Software\\") | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] LegionRelay Telegram / WhatsApp messenger store exfiltration Actions on Objectives High
Hunts LegionRelay's messenger exfiltration capability: non-Telegram / non-WhatsApp processes reading Telegram Desktop's tdata vault or WhatsApp's Local Storage / msgstore. Article explicitly names Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration as core LegionRelay functionality. Rationale: WithSecure explicitly says LegionRelay supports 'Telegram and WhatsApp data exfiltration'. Anchors on the canonical Telegram tdata folder and WhatsApp Desktop Local Storage/IndexedDB layout, gated on non-messenger scripting/archiver parent to keep FP rate low. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1119/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1119 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where FolderPath has_any ("\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\","\\WhatsApp\\Local Storage\\","\\WhatsApp\\IndexedDB\\") or FileName in~ ("key_datas","msgstore.db","map0","map1") | where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe","updater.exe","explorer.exe") | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","7z.exe","winrar.exe") | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$" | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType | order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where TargetFilePath has_any ("\\Telegram Desktop\\tdata\\","\\WhatsApp\\Local Storage\\","\\WhatsApp\\IndexedDB\\") or TargetFileName in~ ("key_datas","msgstore.db") | where ActingProcessName !has_any ("telegram.exe","whatsapp.exe") | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","7z.exe","winrar.exe") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName | order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] GreyVibe: RDP enablement via fDenyTSConnections=0 + firewall by PowerShell RAT Installation High
Hunts LegionRelay's 'RDP access setup' capability: PowerShell or cmd flipping fDenyTSConnections to 0, enabling UserAuthentication, or opening the RDP firewall rule. Article explicitly calls out RDP access setup as a LegionRelay function and the attacker uses PowerShell-based RATs. Rationale: WithSecure: 'LegionRelay supports … RDP access setup.' Anchors on the canonical Windows knobs an attacker has to flip to enable RDP on a previously-disabled host: fDenyTSConnections=0 registry value, UserAuthentication relax, and the RemoteDesktop firewall group. Gated on a scripting-host parent because the article describes the actor as PowerShell-based. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1562/004/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1021.001 T1112 T1562.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry Endpoint.Processes
let RegFlip = DeviceRegistryEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where (RegistryKey has "\\Terminal Server" and RegistryValueName == "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0") or (RegistryKey has "\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValueName == "UserAuthentication") | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","reg.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData; let CmdFlip = DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","netsh.exe","reg.exe") | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("fDenyTSConnections","Set-ItemProperty","Enable-NetFirewallRule","netsh advfirewall") | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Terminal Server","RemoteDesktop","TermService","RDP-Tcp","UserAuthentication") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine; union RegFlip, CmdFlip | order by Timestamp desc
let RegFlip = ImRegistryEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where (RegistryKey has "\\Terminal Server" and RegistryValue == "fDenyTSConnections" and RegistryValueData == "0") or (RegistryKey has "\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp" and RegistryValue == "UserAuthentication") | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","reg.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData; let CmdFlip = SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where EventID == 4688 | where NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","netsh.exe","reg.exe") | where CommandLine has_any ("fDenyTSConnections","Enable-NetFirewallRule","netsh advfirewall","Set-ItemProperty") | where CommandLine has_any ("Terminal Server","RemoteDesktop","TermService","RDP-Tcp","UserAuthentication") | project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine; union RegFlip, CmdFlip | order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:13 (@TargetObject:(*\"Terminal Server"\fDenyTSConnections OR *\"Terminal Server"\WinStations\RDP-Tcp\UserAuthentication) @Details:0)) OR (@EventID:1 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\cmd.exe OR *\netsh.exe OR *\reg.exe) @CommandLine:((*fDenyTSConnections* OR *"Enable-NetFirewallRule"* OR *"netsh advfirewall"*) AND (*"Terminal Server"* OR *RemoteDesktop* OR *RDP-Tcp* OR *UserAuthentication*))))
(#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate (RegObjectName=/\\Terminal Server$/i RegValueName=fDenyTSConnections RegStringValue=0) OR (RegObjectName=/\\WinStations\\RDP-Tcp$/i RegValueName=UserAuthentication)) OR (#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|cmd|netsh|reg)\.exe$/i | regex("(?i)(fDenyTSConnections|Enable-NetFirewallRule|netsh advfirewall)", field=CommandLine) | regex("(?i)(Terminal Server|RemoteDesktop|RDP-Tcp|UserAuthentication)", field=CommandLine)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, RegObjectName], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] PowerShell.exe sustained beaconing to uncategorized web endpoint (LegionRelay/PhantomRelay C2) Command & Control Medium
Hunts the LegionRelay/PhantomRelay PowerShell RAT C2 pattern: powershell.exe making repeated outbound HTTPS connections to a single rare external endpoint with no parent browser. Article describes both RATs as PowerShell-based with web C2 (UTC+3 panels, shared PrincessClub/DroneLink infra). Rationale: Both LegionRelay and PhantomRelay are described as PowerShell RATs and the C2 servers are on UTC+3 with web panels. Threshold + low-cardinality destination expresses 'beaconing' rather than one-shot egress. Doesn't reference specific IOCs from the article on purpose — actor rotates infra — but constrains pivot to powershell.exe initiated egress. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(7d) | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") | where RemotePort in (80,443,8080,8443) | where RemoteIPType == "Public" | summarize ConnectionCount = count(), DistinctRemoteIPs = dcount(RemoteIP), DistinctRemoteUrls = dcount(RemoteUrl), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleUrl = any(RemoteUrl), SampleCmd = any(InitiatingProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 10m) | where ConnectionCount >= 20 and DistinctRemoteIPs <= 2 | order by ConnectionCount desc
ImNetworkSession | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d) | where ActingProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") | where DstPortNumber in (80,443,8080,8443) | summarize ConnectionCount = count(), DistinctIPs = dcount(DstIpAddr), DistinctHosts = dcount(DstHostname), SampleHost = any(DstHostname), SampleCmd = any(ActingProcessCommandLine), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, SrcUsername, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m) | where ConnectionCount >= 20 and DistinctIPs <= 2 | order by ConnectionCount desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @Image:(*\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe) @DestinationPort:(80 OR 443 OR 8080 OR 8443) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 10.0.0.0/8) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 172.16.0.0/12) -CIDR(@DestinationIp, 192.168.0.0/16)

[LLM] GreyVibe cryptocurrency miner deployment via PowerShell RAT Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the cryptominer impact tail of the GreyVibe campaign: known miner binaries (xmrig, ethminer, t-rex, lolMiner) or Stratum protocol egress from victim machines. Article explicitly notes a cryptocurrency miner was deployed on some victim machines. Rationale: WithSecure: 'a cryptocurrency miner was deployed on some victim machines.' Anchors on the well-known XMRig/RandomX family + Stratum protocol strings + canonical mining pool ports (3333/4444/5555/7777/14444) and pool domains. Article didn't ship a specific miner SHA so we rely on family-level indicators. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1496/ • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
ATT&CKT1496

let MinerProcess = DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where FileName in~ ("xmrig.exe","ethminer.exe","t-rex.exe","lolminer.exe","phoenixminer.exe","nbminer.exe","teamredminer.exe","srbminer.exe") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("stratum+tcp://","stratum+ssl://","--algo ","--donate-level","-o stratum","RandomX","--coin=monero","--cpu-priority") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256; let MinerNet = DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where RemotePort in (3333,4444,5555,7777,8333,14444,14433,45700) or RemoteUrl has_any ("pool.minexmr.com","xmrpool","nanopool","f2pool","supportxmr","moneroocean","hashvault","2miners") | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl; union MinerProcess, MinerNet | order by Timestamp desc

title: GreyVibe Cryptocurrency Miner Process or Stratum Egress
id: 2c4d8f01-5e9b-4a17-9b21-8f3c6a1b9d04
description: Detects known cryptominer binaries or Stratum protocol command-lines indicative of GreyVibe's cryptominer impact-stage deployment.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/greyvibe-hackers-use-chatgpt-gemini-to-power-cyberattacks/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/29
tags:
  - attack.t1496
  - attack.impact
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\xmrig.exe'
      - '\ethminer.exe'
      - '\t-rex.exe'
      - '\lolminer.exe'
      - '\phoenixminer.exe'
      - '\nbminer.exe'
      - '\teamredminer.exe'
      - '\srbminer.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'stratum+tcp://'
      - 'stratum+ssl://'
      - '--donate-level'
      - '-o stratum'
      - 'RandomX'
      - '--coin=monero'
  condition: selection_image or selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\xmrig.exe OR *\XMRig.exe OR *\ethminer.exe OR *\"t-rex.exe" OR *\lolminer.exe OR *\phoenixminer.exe OR *\nbminer.exe OR *\teamredminer.exe OR *\srbminer.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*"stratum+tcp://"* OR *"stratum+ssl://"* OR *"--donate-level"* OR *RandomX* OR *"--coin=monero"*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ImageFileName=/(xmrig|ethminer|t-rex|lolminer|phoenixminer|nbminer|teamredminer|srbminer)\.exe$/i OR regex("(?i)(stratum\\+tcp://|stratum\\+ssl://|--donate-level|RandomX|--coin=monero|-o stratum)", field=CommandLine)) | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_name) as process_name values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("xmrig.exe","ethminer.exe","t-rex.exe","lolminer.exe","phoenixminer.exe","nbminer.exe","teamredminer.exe","srbminer.exe") OR Processes.process="*--algo*" OR Processes.process="*stratum+tcp://*" OR Processes.process="*--donate-level*" OR Processes.process="*-o stratum*" OR Processes.process="*xmrig*" OR Processes.process="*RandomX*") by Processes.dest Processes.user _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_name) as process_name values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("xmrig.exe","ethminer.exe","t-rex.exe","lolminer.exe","phoenixminer.exe","nbminer.exe","teamredminer.exe","srbminer.exe") OR Processes.process="*--algo*" OR Processes.process="*stratum+tcp://*" OR Processes.process="*--donate-level*" OR Processes.process="*-o stratum*" OR Processes.process="*xmrig*" OR Processes.process="*RandomX*") by Processes.dest Processes.user _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] BTMOB phishing/C2 domain lookup: arbsniper.com · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] BTMOB Android RAT APK SHA256 observed on managed device · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] BTMOB Android RAT C2 beacon to known infrastructure IPs · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] BTMOB Android RAT C2 beacon to known infrastructure IPs Command & Control High
Detects any corporate-network egress to the BTMOB RAT command-and-control IP set published by ESET and Cyble. BTMOB uses WebSocket-based C2 on these endpoints; a single connection from a managed Android (or any) device is high-fidelity since these IPs serve no legitimate enterprise purpose. Rationale: Direct IOC match against the 8 C2 IPs the article lists. Cross-checked with ESET WeLiveSecurity BTMOB write-up and Cyble's Feb-2025 BTMOB 2.5 analysis — same infrastructure cluster, WebSocket C2 protocol — so these IPs aren't fronting CDNs or shared hosting most enterprises would naturally touch. Defender for Endpoint covers Android too, so DeviceNetworkEvents surfaces the BYOD/MDM-enrolled phone egress as well as desktop hits. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/malware/btmob-stealthy-rat-burrowing-deep-android-devices/ • https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/btmob-android-rat-maas-builder/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1437.001

| where RemoteIP in (BTMOB_C2)

| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, DeviceAction, SourceIP, SourceUserName, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, ApplicationProtocol, RequestURL, ReceivedBytes, SentBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] BTMOB phishing/C2 domain lookup: arbsniper.com Delivery High
Detects DNS resolution or HTTP/S contact with arbsniper.com, the clearnet front for the BTMOB malware-as-a-service identified by ESET. The domain hosts the operator portal and BTMOB lure infrastructure; any enterprise device touching it is either a victim of a phishing redirect or an operator/researcher pivot. Rationale: Single high-confidence domain published in the BleepingComputer article and confirmed as the BTMOB operator portal in ESET's WeLiveSecurity write-up. Domain is exclusive to the MaaS operation — no shared SaaS hosting risk. Covers DNS-layer hits (DnsEvents / ImDnsActivity), egress proxy hits, and Defender's UrlClickEvents so we catch a user clicking the phishing URL out of email as well as on-device beaconing. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/malware/btmob-stealthy-rat-burrowing-deep-android-devices/ • https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1071.001

| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] BTMOB Android RAT APK SHA256 observed on managed device Installation High
Detects file-write, download, or attachment events matching the 8 BTMOB SHA256 hashes published by ESET. Covers BYOD/MDM-enrolled Android endpoints, corporate Windows hosts that may have been used to sideload an APK to a phone via USB, and email attachment scanning. Rationale: Exact-hash IOC match — zero-FP by construction once cross-checked against an authoritative source. Hashes pulled straight from BleepingComputer / ESET write-up and corroborated against Cyble's BTMOB 2.5 sample set. Defender for Endpoint covers Android, so DeviceFileEvents picks up APK drops on enrolled phones; EmailAttachmentInfo covers the email-delivery vector; AlertEvidence catches AV/MDE detonation hits that already triggered. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/malware/btmob-stealthy-rat-burrowing-deep-android-devices/ • https://cyble.com/blog/btmob-rat-newly-discovered-android-malware/ • https://forum.eset.com/topic/49121-btmob-a-stealthy-rat-burrowing-deep-into-android-devices

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07

    object payload signature.
references:

            - '\excel.exe'

            - '\mspub.exe'

            - '\powershell.exe'

            - '\wscript.exe'

            - '\mshta.exe'

level: high

FBI warns of fake FIFA websites running World Cup fraud schemes

BleepingComputer
2026-05-28 9 use cases 2 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

[LLM] DNS/HTTP traffic to Ghost Stadium FIFA typosquat domains (2026 World Cup fraud) Delivery High
Hunts for endpoint resolution or HTTP requests to the eight FIFA look-alike domains called out in the FBI 2026 World Cup PSA and Group-IB's Ghost Stadium reporting. High-fidelity because these hostnames have no legitimate business use. Rationale: Uses the eight specific typosquat hostnames named by the FBI PSA and the Group-IB Ghost Stadium report. Hostnames have no legitimate business use; first-touch is high-fidelity for both DNS and proxy logs.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1189 T1583.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Resolution
let TyposquatDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where RemoteUrl has_any (TyposquatDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountUpn=InitiatingProcessAccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, Source="DeviceNetworkEvents";
let ClickHits = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where Url has_any (TyposquatDomains)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName="", AccountUpn, InitiatingProcessFileName="", RemoteUrl=Url, RemoteIP="", Source="UrlClickEvents";
union NetHits, ClickHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TyposquatDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com"]);
union
(DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where Name has_any (TyposquatDomains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Host=Name, Source="DNS"),
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where RequestURL has_any (TyposquatDomains) or DestinationHostName has_any (TyposquatDomains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Host=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL), Source="Proxy"),
(W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where csReferer has_any (TyposquatDomains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP=cIP, Host=csReferer, Source="IIS-Referer")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Outbound connection to Ghost Stadium FIFA fraud staging IPs Command & Control High
Alerts when any internal host establishes an outbound connection to the eight staging IPs that host the cloned FIFA ticketing/employment/merchandise portals. Catches cases where the typosquat domain was bypassed via direct link, URL shortener, or DNS-over-HTTPS resolution that escaped DNS-tier visibility. Rationale: Targets the eight staging IPs explicitly pre-extracted from the FBI PSA / Group-IB infrastructure tracking. IP-tier detection catches victims who reach the cloned portals via shortened URLs or DoH that bypass DNS visibility.

[LLM] Browser navigation to FIFA-themed look-alike hostname (typosquat pattern hunt) Delivery Medium
Hunting query that surfaces browser traffic to any domain matching the FIFA typosquat pattern family (extra/missing letters, hyphenated subbrands like -hiring/-hr/-careerhub/-ticket, doubled-W prefixes) excluding the legitimate fifa.com/fifa.org. Designed to catch the long tail of the 300+ Ghost Stadium domains beyond the eight in the FBI PSA. Rationale: Article + Group-IB attribution names 300+ Ghost Stadium domains, only 8 of which are pre-extracted. The regex covers the family of typosquat patterns described (homoglyph: fiffa/filfa/f1fa, doubled-W: wvvw-/ww-, sub-brand hyphens: -hiring/-hr/-ticket/-careerhub) while explicitly excluding genuine fifa.com/fifa.org.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1583.001 T1036.005
Data sourcesWeb
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend Hostname = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl)["Host"]))
| where Hostname matches regex @"(fiff[ai]|filfa|f1fa|fifaa|wvvw-?fifa|ww-?fifa|fifa-?(hiring|hr|ticket|tickets|careers?|careerhub|jobs|hospitality|online|com|worldcup|world-cup|2026|store|merch|panini))"
| where Hostname != "fifa.com" and Hostname != "fifa.org" and Hostname !endswith ".fifa.com" and Hostname !endswith ".fifa.org"
| summarize HitCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Devices=dcount(DeviceName), Users=dcount(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn), SampleUrls=make_set(RemoteUrl, 5) by Hostname
| order by FirstSeen desc
let LookalikeRegex = @"(?i)(fiff[ai]|filfa|f1fa|fifaa|wvvw-?fifa|ww-?fifa|fifa-?(hiring|hr|ticket|tickets|careers?|careerhub|jobs|hospitality|online|com|worldcup|world-cup|2026|store|merch|panini))";
union
(CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationHostName matches regex LookalikeRegex or RequestURL matches regex LookalikeRegex | extend Host=tolower(DestinationHostName) | where Host != "fifa.com" and Host != "fifa.org" and Host !endswith ".fifa.com" and Host !endswith ".fifa.org" | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, Host, RequestURL, Source="Proxy"),
(DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name matches regex LookalikeRegex | extend Host=tolower(Name) | where Host != "fifa.com" and Host != "fifa.org" and Host !endswith ".fifa.com" and Host !endswith ".fifa.org" | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP=ClientIP, SourceUserName="", Host, RequestURL="", Source="DNS")
| summarize HitCount=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Sources=dcount(SourceIP) by Host
| order by FirstSeen desc
(@http.url_details.host:*fifa* OR @network.destination.domain:*fifa* OR @dns.question.name:*fifa*) AND -@http.url_details.host:(fifa.com OR www.fifa.com OR fifa.org OR www.fifa.org) AND -@network.destination.domain:(fifa.com OR www.fifa.com OR fifa.org OR www.fifa.org) AND -@dns.question.name:(fifa.com OR www.fifa.com OR fifa.org OR www.fifa.org)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest
| regex("(fiff[ai]|filfa|f1fa|fifaa|wvvw-?fifa|ww-?fifa|fifa-?(hiring|hr|ticket|tickets|careers?|careerhub|jobs|hospitality|online|com|worldcup|world-cup|2026|store|merch|panini))", field=DomainName, flags="i")
| DomainName!=/^(www\.)?fifa\.(com|org)$/i
| groupBy([DomainName], function={ count() | dcount(field=aid, as=hosts) | min(_time, as=firstSeen) })

[LLM] Risky AAD sign-in after user contact with FIFA typosquat phishing portal Actions on Objectives Medium
Correlates users who visited any of the Ghost Stadium FIFA typosquat domains with subsequent risky/anomalous Entra ID sign-ins within 7 days. Targets the post-credential-submission account-takeover pivot described in the article ('create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft'). Rationale: The article explicitly states the harvested PII/credentials are used 'to create fraudulent accounts, commit identity theft'. Joining typosquat visitors against subsequent risky AAD sign-ins is the only way to spot the account-takeover step. The 7-day delay window covers actor lag between data collection and credential reuse.
ATT&CKT1078.004 T1556 T1539
Data sourcesAuthentication Web
let TyposquatDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com"]);
let Visitors = union
    (DeviceNetworkEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where RemoteUrl has_any (TyposquatDomains) | where isnotempty(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn) | project VisitTime=Timestamp, AccountUpn=tolower(InitiatingProcessAccountUpn), DeviceName, VisitedHost=RemoteUrl),
    (UrlClickEvents | where Timestamp > ago(14d) | where Url has_any (TyposquatDomains) | where isnotempty(AccountUpn) | project VisitTime=Timestamp, AccountUpn=tolower(AccountUpn), DeviceName="", VisitedHost=Url);
AADSignInEventsBeta
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where ErrorCode == 0
| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high") or RiskLevelAggregated in ("medium","high") or RiskState in ("atRisk","confirmedCompromised")
| extend AccountUpn=tolower(AccountUpn)
| join kind=inner Visitors on AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (VisitTime .. VisitTime + 7d)
| extend DelayHours = datetime_diff('hour', Timestamp, VisitTime)
| project SignInTime=Timestamp, VisitTime, DelayHours, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Country, City, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskState, Application, VisitedHost, DeviceName
| order by SignInTime desc
let TyposquatDomains = dynamic(["fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com"]);
let Visitors = union
    (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where (RequestURL has_any (TyposquatDomains)) or (DestinationHostName has_any (TyposquatDomains)) | where isnotempty(SourceUserName) | project VisitTime=TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName=tolower(SourceUserName), VisitedHost=coalesce(DestinationHostName,RequestURL)),
    (W3CIISLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d) | where csReferer has_any (TyposquatDomains) | where isnotempty(csUserName) | project VisitTime=TimeGenerated, UserPrincipalName=tolower(csUserName), VisitedHost=csReferer);
SigninLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where ResultType == 0
| where RiskLevelDuringSignIn in ("medium","high") or RiskLevelAggregated in ("medium","high") or RiskState in ("atRisk","confirmedCompromised")
| extend UserPrincipalName=tolower(UserPrincipalName)
| join kind=inner Visitors on UserPrincipalName
| where TimeGenerated between (VisitTime .. VisitTime + 7d)
| extend DelayHours = datetime_diff('hour', TimeGenerated, VisitTime)
| project SignInTime=TimeGenerated, VisitTime, DelayHours, UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, Location, RiskLevelDuringSignIn, RiskState, AppDisplayName, VisitedHost
| order by SignInTime desc
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(fiffa\.com|jobs-fifa\.com|fifa-hiring\.com|filfa\.org|wvvw-fifa\.com|ww-fifa\.com|fifa-hr\.com|fifa-careerhub\.com)$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=IdpAuthenticationLog RiskLevel=/medium|high/i EventResult=success}, field=[aid], include=[UserPrincipal, RemoteIp, RiskLevel, _time])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserPrincipal, DomainName, RiskLevel], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Web where (Web.dest IN ("fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com")) by Web.user, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename _time as visitTime user as visitor | join visitor [| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.action=success AND (Authentication.signature="risky" OR Authentication.signature="highRisk" OR Authentication.signature="mediumRisk")) by Authentication.user, Authentication.src, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as visitor _time as signinTime] | where signinTime >= visitTime AND signinTime <= visitTime + 604800 | eval delaySec = signinTime - visitTime | table visitTime, signinTime, delaySec, visitor, src
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web where (Web.dest IN ("fiffa.com","jobs-fifa.com","fifa-hiring.com","filfa.org","wvvw-fifa.com","ww-fifa.com","fifa-hr.com","fifa-careerhub.com")) by Web.user, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rename _time as visitTime user as visitor | join visitor [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Authentication where (Authentication.action=success AND (Authentication.signature="risky" OR Authentication.signature="highRisk" OR Authentication.signature="mediumRisk")) by Authentication.user, Authentication.src, _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)` | rename user as visitor _time as signinTime] | where signinTime >= visitTime AND signinTime <= visitTime + 604800 | eval delaySec = signinTime - visitTime | table visitTime, signinTime, delaySec, visitor, src
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject

Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or SHA1 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a") or MD5 in~ ("3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["3b8bb7631b39f455d31544b55ba97b49ab1888c1", "84ecdca915f1af822ccc8a04479f5179104f353c", "9bd164dd3f50d196c7dff4f6c1b0f1345ac96d9a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:

            - '\Program Files (x86)\'

falsepositives:

      article before alerting.
level: medium
